chunks: From him, from Al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Masoudi, from Hafs ibn Umar al-Bajali, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about my state and the breakdown of my affairs upon me. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you arrive in Kufa, sell a pillow from your house for ten dirhams, and invite your brethren, and prepare food for them, and ask them to supplicate to Allah for you.'

He (the narrator) said, 'So I did, and that was not possible for me until I had sold a pillow, and I prepared food just as he had ordered me to, and I asked them to supplicate to Allah for me.' He said, 'By Allah, I did not remain for long until a debtor of mine came to me, knocked on my door, and reconciled with me from some wealth of mine which was a lot. I had reckoned it to be approximately ten thousand dirhams.' He said, 'Then the affairs turned towards me (in my favor).'

key_terms.أَقْبَلَتِ الْأَشْيَاءُ: affairs turned towards me / things improved

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual remedy for financial distress according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia principle of *sabr* combined with practical action, where Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Hafs ibn Umar to prioritize social bonds and communal supplication (*du'a*) over hoarding wealth. The narrative highlights the spiritual efficacy of inviting kin (*silat al-rahim*) and the immediate divine response to sincere reliance on God, transforming perceived scarcity into abundance through blessing (*barakah*).

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Abbas Bin Aamir, from Abu Abdul Rahman Al Masoudi, from Hafs Bin Umar Al Bajaly who said,

‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> of my state and the breakdown of my affairs upon me. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘When you proceed to Al-Kufa, so sell a pillow from your house for ten Dirhams and invite your brethren, and prepare a meal for them, and ask them to be supplicating to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for you’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did, and that was not possible for me until I had to sell a pillow, and I took some food just as he<sup>asws</sup> had ordered me to, and I asked them that they should supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for me. So, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, it was not except for a little while until a debtor came over to me, so he knocked upon the door to me, and reconciled with me from some wealth for me which was a lot. I had reckoned it to be approximately ten thousand Dirham. Then the things turned towards me (in my favour)’.
en.sarwar: 41. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Haytham ibn abu Masruq al-Nahdiy from Musa ibn ‘Umar ibn Bazi’ who has said the following:

“I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, people narrate that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, whenever he walked on a road would not return from the same, if this is how it was. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, that is how it was and very often I also do so and you should also do it.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘It gives you a greater chance to increase your sustenance.’”
